plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Bare branches break into clouds of fragrant blossoms. The flowers are small and almost papery, and they open while winter's chill still lingers. Their sweet, spicy scent drifts through orchards and temple gardens well before most other trees stir.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late January to March, peaking in late winter
plants.location: Japan, China and other parts of temperate East Asia, in orchards, parks and gardens
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms have long symbolized perseverance in East Asian culture, because they flower in the cold before spring has fully arrived. The same trees later produce the sour fruits used for umeboshi pickles and plum wine.

plants.name: Prunus campanulata
plants.description: This small, graceful tree is covered in nodding, bell-shaped blooms of intense rose-red. The flowers hang in jewel-toned clusters. Unlike the pale blossoms of many cherries, they make a bold splash of color in the late-winter landscape.
plants.location: Warm-climate gardens such as the southern United States, where it is grown as an early flowering cherry. It is native to Taiwan and southern East Asia.
plants.funFact: Its flowers hang downward like little bells, which gives the species its name. Its blooms appear much earlier than those of most flowering cherries, so it often opens in the warmth of late winter.
